clue.text: Carrier gets dismissal after time's lost in traffic

indicators.note: after places the dismissal word behind the trimmed traffic word
lost says the letter for time goes missing from the word for traffic

parts.note: truck is an old word for dealings or traffic, as in 'have no truck with'
T is the standard abbreviation for time
the sack is dismissal from a job

explanation.surface: Someone loses their job and their time after being caught in a traffic jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traffic' looks like cars on the road, but it is the old sense of dealings, as in 'have no truck with'. 'Lost' drops the time letter and 'after' sets the dismissal behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack is a bag for carrying belongings on the back, so it is a carrier.

clue.text: Recipe beginning with a brie cooked on toast, initially?

definitions.text: Recipe beginning with a brie cooked on toast, initially?

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin 'recipe', take

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of the cheese are mixed up
initially picks the opening letter of toast

explanation.surface: A recipe starts with some brie melted on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: R (recipe) comes first, then A, then BRIE rearranged by 'cooked' to make REBI, and the first letter of toast from 'initially'. The whole clue also describes the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is melted cheese on toast, a dish like brie cooked on toast.

clue.text: Feature about military alliance with ethnic enclave

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: about tells us to move the following letters around

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature covers a military alliance with an ethnic community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' looks like an article but is the CHIN. 'About' rearranges NATO and W (with) into ATOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinatown is a district of a city where Chinese people live and trade, an ethnic quarter.

clue.text: Weapon Japanese commander used to hold leader in Tokyo

indicators.note: used to hold says the commander's title wraps around the next letter

parts.note: a shogun was a hereditary Japanese military commander

indicators.note: leader in picks the opening letter of Tokyo

explanation.surface: A Japanese general held a weapon to the head of his leader in Tokyo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used to hold' puts T, the first letter of Tokyo ('leader in'), inside SHOGUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is a firearm firing shot, a weapon.

clue.text: Is inclined, in church, to 'clear of guilt

indicators.note: in places the leaning word inside the letters for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
leans means is inclined

explanation.surface: Someone tends to go to church to be cleared of guilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the container. The apostrophe before 'clear' is a stray quote mark in the printed clue and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse someone is to purify or free them, as of sin or guilt.

clue.text: Loud and blaring sound heard in club

indicators.note: sound heard says the word for the club is said aloud and the answer matches it

parts.note: a brassie is an old name for a golf club, a wooden two-wood

explanation.surface: A noisy, blaring din is heard inside a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a nightclub, but it is BRASSIE, an old golf club. 'Sound heard' says it is spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassy describes harsh, strident noise like brass instruments, hence loud and blaring.

clue.text: A star first needs to manage dance

parts.note: to boss is to manage or direct
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A celebrity first needs someone to manage her dancing career.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists 'A star' first, but 'first needs to manage' asks for the managing word to come first, before A and the star.
explanation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian dance rhythm related to samba.

clue.text: Tell a couple of pages to get up

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page, so two pages are PP
to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: A pair of page boys are told to get out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is the usual written abbreviation for pages.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprise someone is to inform them, to tell them.

clue.text: Chap taking new, not quite chilled, tinny?

parts.note: Stan is a man's name, standing for any chap

indicators.note: not quite removes the final letter of the chilled word

parts.note: icy means very chilled

explanation.surface: A fellow grabs a can of beer that is not quite cold enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims ICY to IC. 'Tinny' is Australian slang for a can of beer, but here it means made of tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Stannic is the chemical adjective for compounds of tin, from Latin stannum, so tinny in a literal sense.

clue.text: What might get sore horn in charge if it all goes wrong

definitions.text: What might get sore horn in charge if it all goes wrong

indicators.note: if it all goes wrong tells us to rearrange the preceding letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A creature might end up with a painful horn if a charge goes badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If it all goes wrong' rearranges SORE HORN with IC (in charge). The whole clue also describes the beast: a charging rhino could well bruise its horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhino is the horned animal famous for charging, which could hurt its horn.

clue.text: Carriage for one setting out on journey of a lifetime

definitions.text: Carriage for one setting out on journey of a lifetime

parts.words: Carriage for one setting out on journey of a lifetime
parts.note: the one setting out on life's journey is a newborn baby, and its carriage is the wheeled vehicle it is pushed in

explanation.surface: A grand coach is booked for a traveller's once-in-a-lifetime trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'journey of a lifetime' sounds like a holiday, but it is life itself, begun by a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A pram is the wheeled carriage in which a baby is pushed about.

clue.text: Old drop-outs given responsibility for rhythm section?

definitions.meaning: the 1950s literary bohemians who rejected mainstream society
read literally, the producing of the beat, which is what a rhythm section is responsible for

explanation.surface: Retired dropouts are put in charge of a band's drums and bass.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the phrase literally: generating the beat is the job of a band's rhythm section.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beat Generation were the 1950s American writers and bohemians who rejected conventional society, early drop-outs.

clue.text: Beat soundly in counter-move?

indicators.note: move, attached to the word before it, tells us to shift those letters about

explanation.surface: A hefty win is gained with a counter-move in a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter-move' looks like one word for a reply in chess, but 'move' is an anagram signal working on COUNTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce someone is to defeat them heavily, to beat them soundly.

clue.text: Explorer covering river in rapid survey

indicators.note: covering, in a down clue, puts the explorer above the river

parts.note: Captain James Cook was the British explorer of the Pacific
the Stour is a river in southern England

explanation.surface: A traveller takes a fast trip along a river to make a survey.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer one piece 'covering' another sits on top of it. A Cook's tour, from Thomas Cook's travel firm, is a quick look round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cook's tour is a brief, hurried tour of the main sights, so a quick overview.

clue.text: Drama producer's new version of Cosi with ENO?

indicators.note: a new version of the words suggests rearranging their letters

parts.note: ENO is the English National Opera, which might stage Mozart's Cosi fan tutte

explanation.surface: English National Opera stages a fresh production of Mozart's Cosi.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about opera, but the dramatist is the absurdist playwright. 'New version of' rearranges COSI and ENO.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene Ionesco was a Romanian-French playwright, so he produced drama.

clue.text: Ascertain how it might be represented as bigoted

indicators.note: how the word might be represented means its letters can be shown in another order

explanation.surface: A survey asks how prejudice might be portrayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How it might be represented' rearranges the letters of ASCERTAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectarian means narrowly bound to one sect and hostile to others, so bigoted.

clue.text: Brunel's nominal predecessor in England, say

definitions.meaning: the name before Brunel in his full name
England is an example of a realm ruled by a monarch

explanation.surface: Before the great engineer came along, England stood waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: Isambard Kingdom Brunel was the Victorian British engineer of bridges, railways and ships; his middle name precedes his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: England is a realm under a monarch, an example of a monarchy's territory.

clue.text: As an alternative this month, last parts of puzzle extra hard

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means of this month in old business letters

indicators.note: last parts of picks the final letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: This month's crossword has an extra-hard ending as a change.
explanation.walkthrough: INST is old commercial shorthand for 'this month'. 'Last parts of' gives E, A, D from puzzle, extra, hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead means in place of something else, as a substitute.

clue.text: Brave impudence shown by soldier, perhaps

parts.note: gall is cheek or impudence
a soldier is one caste of ant, so an ant is an example

explanation.surface: A soldier shows bold cheek and courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' is a soldier ant, hence the 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant means courageous and spirited, a synonym of brave.

clue.text: Full partner's fair share

definitions.meaning: an equal partner takes fifty per cent of the takings

explanation.surface: A business partner wants a full and fair share of the profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full' means drunk here; half-cut is British slang for tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-cut is informal British slang for being drunk, and full is slang with the same meaning.

clue.text: Courageous woman needing combination of drugs

parts.note: heroin is a drug
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A brave woman needs a cocktail of medicines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combination of drugs' supplies two: HEROIN plus E, short for ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A heroine is a woman admired for bravery.

clue.text: Boy holding map showing where Father Christmas lives?

indicators.note: holding means the boy word wraps around the map word

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a plan is a map or diagram

explanation.surface: A child holds a map showing the way to Santa's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' signals the container. The question mark admits Santa's home is a tradition, not a fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapland, in northern Finland, is the legendary home of Santa Claus.

clue.text: City of France following the heartless period of occupation

indicators.note: following places the French city after the trimmed word
heartless removes the middle letter of the word given

parts.note: Nancy is a city in north-eastern France

explanation.surface: A French city endured a cruel period of occupation by an enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle letter of 'the'; 'following' places the French city after what is left. Nancy is the capital of historic Lorraine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the time during which a tenant occupies property.

clue.text: Prime Minister requiring simple location for historic monument

parts.note: Lord Salisbury was a British Prime Minister three times in the late Victorian era
plain means simple or unadorned

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister wants a modest site for a historic memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: The monument is Stonehenge, which stands on this chalk plateau in Wiltshire, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonehenge, the prehistoric stone circle, stands on this Wiltshire plateau.

clue.text: Her daughter had to be brought back from Paris

definitions.text: Her daughter had to be brought back from Paris

parts.words: Her daughter had to be brought back from Paris
parts.note: the daughter is Helen of Troy, abducted by the Trojan prince Paris, not the French capital, and recovered by the Greeks

explanation.surface: A mother's girl ran off to the French capital and had to be fetched home.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is the Trojan prince, not the French city: he carried off Helen, whose mother was seduced by Zeus as a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this queen of Sparta was the mother of Helen, whom Paris took to Troy.

clue.text: Soldier is backward in offering duty

indicators.note: in places the turned soldier inside the word for offering

parts.note: an oblation is a religious offering

indicators.note: backward says the soldier's letters are read right to left

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is reluctant to make his contribution to his duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' turns the American soldier round, and 'in' sets him inside the religious offering.
explanation.definitionFit: An obligation is something one is bound to do, a duty.

clue.text: The last person you'd expect to have worked on this puzzle

definitions.text: The last person you'd expect to have worked on this puzzle

parts.words: The last person you'd expect to have worked on this puzzle
parts.note: sounds like the least likely solver, but means the final person to handle the puzzle before publication

explanation.surface: Whoever did this crossword was the least likely candidate of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last person you'd expect' reads as 'most unlikely', but it means literally the final one: the person who checks a crossword before it is printed.
explanation.definitionFit: The newspaper official who checks the crossword last before printing is the one who prepares copy for publication.

clue.text: A number refuse to conceal Conservative leaning

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: to conceal means the refusal word wraps around the Conservative letter

parts.note: to deny is to refuse

explanation.surface: Several people refuse to hide their Tory sympathies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To conceal' has the refusal word wrapping the Conservative abbreviation, all after the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency is an inclination toward something, a leaning.
